findings.title: Any authenticated wallet can exhaust the example's global agent spend cap
findings.description: The page instructs users to enable wallet authentication for keypair data commands, but the spend policy authorizes create for every non-null @user.id. Wallet authentication establishes identity, not ownership of the agent or app, so any unrelated wallet able to sign in can append a caller-selected amount. Because the rollingSum has no scopeVariable, all writers share the same cap. An attacker can submit one amount-100 record, poison the spend ledger, and deny the legitimate agent all writes for the next hour. The referenced invariants documentation explicitly warns that this exact unbound pattern permits cap-exhaustion denial of service.
findings.recommendation: For a single-agent backend, bind create to a constant containing that agent's authenticated @user.id. For multiple agents, use a path such as agents/$agentId/spend/$entryId, require $agentId to equal the caller or a verified membership entry, and set scopeVariable to $agentId. Derive amount in trusted backend code when it represents real cost rather than accepting it from the client.
